content.user_title: Build Native iOS Apps With Swift
content.value_statement: Native iOS development requires platform knowledge across UI, data, security, testing, and App Store release work. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused guidance for Swift-first iOS implementation.
actual_capabilities: Plans SwiftUI-first features with UIKit integration when existing code needs it.
Guides persistence choices using Core Data, SwiftData, CloudKit, Keychain, and file storage.
Recommends networking patterns with URLSession, async await, Codable, GraphQL, and WebSocket support.
Covers testing with XCTest, XCUITest, snapshot testing, performance testing, and TestFlight workflows.
Adds iOS security, privacy, accessibility, and App Store review considerations to implementation plans.
Advises on Apple ecosystem features such as widgets, Live Activities, Watch connectivity, and iCloud.
limitations: It provides guidance and generated implementation plans, but it cannot run Xcode or sign builds by itself.
It does not replace Apple documentation review for changed APIs or App Store policy updates.
It needs project context before recommending migrations, architecture changes, or dependency choices.
It may reference optional tools such as Fastlane, Sentry, or Apollo that a project may not use.

use_cases.title: Create a SwiftUI Feature
use_cases.description: Design a new iOS screen with state management, navigation, error handling, accessibility, and tests.

use_cases.title: Modernize a Legacy Module
use_cases.description: Plan a safe migration from UIKit or older Swift patterns toward SwiftUI, Combine, and modular architecture.

use_cases.title: Prepare for App Store Release
use_cases.description: Review privacy, performance, metadata, TestFlight, screenshots, and App Store review risks before submission.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an iOS Feature
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new feature plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an iOS feature for [feature goal]. Use SwiftUI where appropriate. Include data flow, screens, accessibility, testing, and App Store concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Review SwiftUI Architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for project structure feedback.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this iOS architecture: [paste summary]. Recommend SwiftUI state management, navigation, dependency injection, persistence, and test improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Secure API Integration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for networking and privacy guidance.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a secure iOS API integration for [service]. Cover URLSession, Codable models, authentication storage, retries, offline behavior, privacy, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Release Readiness Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request before TestFlight or App Store submission.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this iOS release plan: [paste details]. Check performance, accessibility, privacy labels, App Store review risks, TestFlight, crash reporting, and rollback planning.

output_examples.input: Build a SwiftUI profile editor with local persistence.
output_examples.output: A feature plan covering screens, view models, SwiftData storage, validation states, accessibility labels, unit tests, and UI test coverage.

output_examples.input: Migrate an old UIKit settings screen to SwiftUI.
output_examples.output: A migration strategy with wrapper boundaries, navigation changes, state ownership, rollout steps, regression tests, and fallback handling.

output_examples.input: Prepare my app for TestFlight and App Store review.
output_examples.output: A release checklist covering signing, build configuration, privacy labels, screenshots, crash reporting, beta feedback, metadata, and review guideline risks.

best_practices: Share the target iOS version, Xcode version, current architecture, and important dependencies before asking for implementation guidance.
Ask for accessibility, privacy, error handling, and test coverage with every user-facing feature.
Validate generated code against Apple documentation and project build settings before release.
anti_patterns: Do not request broad rewrites without describing existing modules, risks, and release constraints.
Do not store tokens, passwords, or personal data outside secure iOS storage mechanisms.
Do not treat App Store or privacy guidance as legal approval without separate review.

faq.question: What iOS work does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Swift, SwiftUI, UIKit integration, persistence, networking, testing, performance, privacy, accessibility, and release planning.

faq.question: Can it generate Swift code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide Swift implementation, but you should compile and test the result in Xcode.

faq.question: Does it replace Apple documentation?
faq.answer: No. Use Apple documentation for final API details, policy changes, and release requirements.

faq.question: Can it help with legacy UIKit apps?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan UIKit maintenance, SwiftUI migration, and hybrid architectures.

faq.question: Does it cover App Store optimization?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help with metadata, screenshots, review readiness, privacy labels, TestFlight, and release checks.

faq.question: What context should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide project goals, iOS target version, current architecture, dependencies, user flows, and release constraints.
